Hypergraph eigenvector centralities

Source: R/hypergraph_centrality.R
hypergraph_centrality.Rd

hypergraph_centrality() scores how central each node of a hypergraph is, with up to three eigenvector centralities from Benson (2019): clique-motif (CEC, "clique"), Z-eigenvector (ZEC, "Z") and H-eigenvector (HEC, "H"). CEC flattens the groups into pairs by clique expansion and takes the eigenvector centrality of that pairwise graph. ZEC and HEC work on the hyperedges directly: a node's score grows with the product of the scores of the other members of each hyperedge it belongs to. It reads a net_hypergraph from build_hypergraph() or bipartite_groups().

The variants can rank the nodes differently, since CEC counts shared memberships pair by pair while ZEC and HEC weigh each group as a whole. ZEC and HEC are defined for uniform hypergraphs only, where every hyperedge of two or more members has the same size. On a disconnected hypergraph, compare scores within one component: CEC gives zero to every component whose leading eigenvalue is below the largest, and the Z-eigenvector is not unique. hypergraph_measures() describes the structure the scores come from.

Usage

hypergraph_centrality(
  hg,
  type = "clique",
  max_iter = 1000L,
  tol = 1e-08,
  normalize = TRUE
)

Arguments

hg

The hypergraph: a net_hypergraph from build_hypergraph() or bipartite_groups().

type

The centralities to compute, any of "clique", "Z" and "H", returned in the order given. Default "clique". "Z" and "H" need a uniform hypergraph (every hyperedge with two or more members has the same size); on any other they raise an error of class nestimate_nonuniform_hypergraph.

max_iter

The largest number of power-iteration steps for "Z" and "H". Default 1000. "clique" is solved directly and ignores it.

tol

The convergence tolerance for "Z" and "H": the iteration stops once the L1 change between successive iterates is below it. Default 1e-8. An iteration that does not get there within max_iter steps, or that stops without solving the eigen-equation, warns with class nestimate_no_converge.

normalize

How each vector is scaled. TRUE (default) gives it unit Euclidean (L2) norm; FALSE divides it by its largest absolute entry, so the top node scores 1, the scale of igraph::eigen_centrality().

Value

A named list with one numeric vector per requested type, in the order given, each with one value per node of hg, named by the nodes. A hypergraph with no hyperedges, or with only one-member hyperedges, gives all-zero vectors, and one without nodes empty vectors.

Details

Clique-motif eigenvector centrality (CEC) is the leading eigenvector of the clique-expanded pairwise graph \(W\) with \(W_{ij} = |\{e : i, j \in e\}|\), the number of hyperedges two nodes share. It reads membership only, so incidence weights are ignored: it equals igraph::eigen_centrality() on clique_expansion(hg, weighted = FALSE), and on clique_expansion()'s default output only for an unweighted hypergraph. The vector is solved directly from a symmetric eigendecomposition of each connected component (Perron-Frobenius makes the leading eigenvalue of a connected component simple), not by power iteration, which oscillates when the clique expansion is bipartite (for example a star of pairs). When several components share the largest eigenvalue, the result is the projection of the uniform vector onto their joint leading eigenspace; components with a smaller leading eigenvalue score zero.

Z-eigenvector centrality (ZEC) solves the eigen-equation on the hyperedge tensor, $$\lambda\, x_i \;=\; \sum_{e \ni i}\; \prod_{j \in e,\; j \neq i} x_j,$$ by a shifted power iteration (a variant of SS-HOPM, Kolda & Mayo, 2011, that normalises the tensor step before adding the shift). Tensor products and normalisation are evaluated in log space, so the centralities stay finite and normalised for large hyperedges. Besides the step tolerance, the iteration checks that the eigen-equation residual is small (relative residual at most max(sqrt(tol), 1e-6)); otherwise it warns.

H-eigenvector centrality (HEC) solves, by the same iteration, $$\lambda\, x_i^{k-1} \;=\; \sum_{e \ni i}\; \prod_{j \in e,\; j \neq i} x_j.$$

Uniform hypergraphs only. Benson (2019) defines ZEC and HEC for \(k\)-uniform hypergraphs. With mixed sizes the right-hand side mixes polynomial degrees, so the equation has no scale-free solution: the vector satisfies it only at the normalisation chosen inside the iteration. Hyperedges with one member contribute nothing and are ignored by the uniformity check. For mixed sizes use "clique", or keep one size with build_hypergraph() (include_pairwise = FALSE).

Disconnected hypergraphs. The Z-eigenvector is not unique when the hypergraph has several components: different iterations can solve the equation with different vectors, so compare "Z" values within one connected hypergraph only.

Note

The "clique" (CEC) variant is validated against igraph::eigen_centrality() (cosine ~ 1). The "Z" and "H" variants are experimental: they are validated only against a clean-room list-based tensor power iteration (the same operator with a different loop structure), as no R package exposes tensor eigenvectors for an independent comparison.

References

Benson, A. R. (2019). Three hypergraph eigenvector centralities. SIAM Journal on Mathematics of Data Science 1(2), 293-312. arXiv:1807.09644.

Kolda, T. G., & Mayo, J. R. (2011). Shifted power method for computing tensor eigenpairs. SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications 32(4), 1095-1124. doi:10.1137/100801482

See also

build_hypergraph(), clique_expansion(), hypergraph_measures().

Examples

df <- data.frame(
  player  = c("A", "B", "C", "A", "B", "D", "C", "D", "E"),
  session = c("S1", "S1", "S1", "S2", "S2", "S3", "S3", "S3", "S3")
)
hg <- bipartite_groups(df, "player", "session")
hypergraph_centrality(hg)
#> $clique
#>         A         B         C         D         E 
#> 0.5345225 0.5345225 0.5345225 0.2672612 0.2672612 
#> 

# Z and H need a uniform hypergraph: here every session has three players
df3 <- data.frame(
  player  = c("A", "B", "C", "A", "B", "D", "C", "D", "E"),
  session = c("S1", "S1", "S1", "S2", "S2", "S2", "S3", "S3", "S3")
)
hypergraph_centrality(bipartite_groups(df3, "player", "session"),
                      type = c("clique", "Z", "H"))
#> $clique
#>         A         B         C         D         E 
#> 0.5127870 0.5127870 0.4559848 0.4559848 0.2413603 
#> 
#> $Z
#>         A         B         C         D         E 
#> 0.5345225 0.5345225 0.4364358 0.4364358 0.2182179 
#> 
#> $H
#>         A         B         C         D         E 
#> 0.4867656 0.4867656 0.4556438 0.4556438 0.3330103 
#>
